topicName: Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and Elastic Pools
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and Elastic Pools"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Microsoft Azure offers multiple relational database-as-a-service (DBaaS) options built on the SQL Server engine. Choosing the right deployment model depends on your application architecture, migration requirements, and cost management strategy."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Azure SQL Database"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure SQL Database is a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS) database engine that handles most database management functions such as upgrading, patching, backups, and monitoring without user involvement. It is ideal for modern cloud applications that want to use the latest relational database capabilities."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Azure SQL Managed Instance"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure SQL Managed Instance is a fully managed instance of SQL Server that provides near 100% compatibility with the SQL Server (Enterprise Edition) database engine. It includes native virtual network (VNet) support and simplifies the migration of on-premises SQL Server databases to the cloud without application rewrites."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Azure SQL Elastic Pools"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Elastic pools are a simple, cost-effective solution for managing and scaling multiple databases that have varying and unpredictable usage demands. The databases in an elastic pool are on a single Azure SQL Database server and share a set of resources for a set price."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Deployment Example using Azure CLI"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following Azure CLI script demonstrates how to create an Azure SQL logical server, configure an elastic pool, and deploy a database into that pool."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"az group create --name "rg-sqltutorial-prod" --location "eastus"

az sql server create --name "sqlserver-demo-prod" --resource-group "rg-sqltutorial-prod" --admin-user "sqladmin" --admin-password "P@ssw0rd12345!"

az sql elastic-pool create --resource-group "rg-sqltutorial-prod" --server "sqlserver-demo-prod" --name "PoolBasic" --edition "GeneralPurpose" --family "Gen5" --capacity 2

az sql db create --resource-group "rg-sqltutorial-prod" --server "sqlserver-demo-prod" --name "mydatabase1" --elastic-pool "PoolBasic""},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Architectural Considerations"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Azure SQL Database for cloud-native applications requiring single-database isolation or elastic pooling."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Azure SQL Managed Instance for legacy applications requiring SQL Server Agent, cross-database queries, CLR integration, or database sizes up to 16 TB."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Elastic Pools when managing multiple SaaS databases with fluctuating workloads to optimize resource utilization and reduce overall cloud expenditure."}]
